s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative corneal inflammation with stromal lesions
salient_findings: Brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
Central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on optical coherence tomography
Peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma on optical coherence tomography
key_facts: 68-year-old man with pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
Underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
History of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months before DSAEK
Postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
Referred for evaluation of keratitis in the right eye 2 months after DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
No pain with ocular movements
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showed brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal

shortlist.label: Exophiala xenobiotica keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma and history of previous eye infection suggest fungal etiology

shortlist.label: Fungal keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Postoperative corneal inflammation with stromal lesions is consistent with fungal infection

shortlist.label: Scedosporium keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Exophiala, Scedosporium can cause fungal keratitis with stromal involvement

shortlist.label: Fusarium keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fusarium is a common cause of fungal keratitis, especially in postoperative or contact lens-related cases

shortlist.label: Aspergillus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aspergillus is another common fungal pathogen that can cause keratitis with stromal lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma and the patient's history of corticosteroid use are consistent with Exophiala xenobiotica keratitis, which is a rare but recognized cause of fungal keratitis, particularly in immunocompromised patients or those on long-term corticosteroid therapy.

rejected.label: Fungal keratitis
rejected.why: Too broad, as the vignette suggests a specific type of fungal keratitis

rejected.label: Scedosporium keratitis
rejected.why: No specific evidence in the vignette to support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Fusarium keratitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more severe symptoms and a different clinical appearance

rejected.label: Aspergillus keratitis
rejected.why: Not specifically suggested by the clinical findings or the patient's history
